strings.hist_tagline: Four thousand years on Albay Gulf, from the fishing village of Sawangan to the regional capital of Bicol.
strings.hist_brief_title: The Story of Legazpi, in Brief
strings.hist_brief1_desc: Archaeological evidence from the Mataas Shell Scoop and Hoyop-Hoyopan Cave proves early trade across the Pacific.
strings.hist_brief2_desc: The 1814 Mayon eruption separated inland Albay Nuevo and coastal Binanuahan, creating the dual-center urban layout seen today.
strings.hist_brief3_desc: Legazpi earned city charters in 1892 (Becerra Law), 1948 (RA 306), and definitively on June 12, 1959 under Republic Act 2234.
strings.hist_tl1_desc: Earliest archaeological artifact in Albay Gulf; ancient seafaring networks.
strings.hist_tl2_desc: Franciscans establish the first chapel dedicated to St. Gregory the Great.
strings.hist_tl3_desc: Elevated to capital of the sprawling Partido de Ibalón colonial province.
strings.hist_tl4_desc: 1,200 casualties; survivors rebuild Albay Nuevo inland and Binanuahan on the coast.
strings.hist_tl5_desc: Royal Decree officially christens the town; Don Lorenzo Hao becomes 1st Gobernadorcillo.
strings.hist_tl6_desc: First city status uniting Legazpi Port, Albay, and Daraga into one Ayuntamiento.
strings.hist_tl7_desc: Fierce Philippine-American War action at San Rafael Bridge led by Gen. Paua.
strings.hist_tl8_desc: U.S. 158th RCT and Bicolano guerrillas liberate the ruined port district.
strings.hist_tl9_desc: Permanent cityhood chartered; Mayor Ramon A. Arnaldo serves as first city mayor.
strings.hist_tl10_desc: Presidential Decree No. 1 designates Legazpi the administrative hub of Region V.
strings.hist_tl11_desc: Pioneering first permanent provincial disaster risk reduction office in the nation.
strings.hist_tl12_desc: Modern international gateway opens; commercial expansion accelerates.
strings.hist_tl13_desc: Mayor Hisham Ismail leads push toward Highly Urbanized City status.

strings.faq_a3: The City Hall is open Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, with a lunch break from 12:00 PM to 1:00 PM. It is closed on weekends and on national and local holidays.
strings.faq_a5: Some can. Business permit applications and renewals, business billing, and real property tax billing and payment can be started online through the city's Filipizen portal. Building permit and certificate of occupancy applications have published step-by-step guides, but you still complete them in person. Most other services are still in person only. Each service category page lists what is available online for that category, and says plainly whether a link is a working portal, a guide, or a payment channel.
strings.faq_a6: For birth certificates registered in Legazpi City, it typically takes 15-30 minutes while you wait, provided the record is readily available.
strings.faq_a7_li1: An authorization letter signed by you
strings.faq_a7_li2: Valid ID of both you and the representative
strings.faq_a8: Both are certified true copies. PSA certificates are the nationally-recognized version required for passport and visa applications. Local civil registrar certificates are accepted for most local transactions and are often processed faster.
strings.faq_a9: Business permits must be renewed annually, preferably in January. The deadline for penalty-free renewal is typically January 20th of each year.
strings.faq_a10_intro: To start a new business, you'll need:
strings.faq_a10_li1: DTI Registration (for sole proprietorship) or SEC Registration (for corporation)
strings.faq_a11: The City Treasurer's Office accepts cash payments in person. Real property tax and business billing can also be paid online through the city's Filipizen portal. Fees for individual services are listed on that service's page, taken from the city's published Citizen's Charter.
strings.faq_a12: Visit the City Treasurer's Office at the City Hall with your Tax Declaration or latest Official Receipt. Payment is in cash. Property taxes are due quarterly, but you may pay annually to avail of discounts.
strings.faq_a13_intro: Go to the City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWDO) with:
strings.faq_a13_li1: Birth Certificate or any valid ID showing your age (60 and above)
strings.faq_a13_outro: The ID is issued for free.
strings.faq_a14: Senior citizens enjoy 20% discount and VAT exemption on purchases (with a minimum purchase amount per establishment), priority lanes, and access to special programs and medical assistance from the municipality.

strings.a11y_tagline: Our commitment to digital accessibility for all citizens
strings.a11y_commitment_text: BetterLegazpi is committed to ensuring digital accessibility for people with disabilities. We aim for WCAG 2.1 Level AA across the whole site and test every page against it automatically, in both themes and at phone and desktop widths. We describe the site as partially conformant rather than conformant, because a few pages still fail that standard. They are listed under Known Limitations below, and naming them is how we hold ourselves to fixing them.
strings.a11y_feat1_desc: All functionality available using only a keyboard.
strings.a11y_feat2_desc: Compatible with JAWS, NVDA, and VoiceOver.
strings.a11y_feat3_desc: All images have descriptive alt text.
strings.a11y_feat4_desc: Text meets WCAG AA contrast on all but the pages named under Known Limitations.
strings.a11y_feat5_desc: Works on all devices and screen sizes.
strings.a11y_feat6_desc: No time limits on reading or interacting.
strings.a11y_limitations_intro: We test every page of this site automatically against WCAG 2.1 Level A and AA, in both light and dark themes and at both phone and desktop widths. These are the pages that do not pass yet, as of August 29, 2026:
strings.a11y_limit_pdfs: Documents we link to that are published by other offices, mainly PDFs, are outside our control and are often not readable by screen readers.
strings.a11y_limit_embeds: Content embedded from other sites, such as posts from the city's Facebook page, follows that site's accessibility, not ours.
strings.a11y_limitations_outro: Everything else we test passes. If you find a problem that is not listed here, please tell us using the contact details below: an unlisted problem is one we do not know about.
strings.a11y_alt_text: If you encounter difficulty accessing any information, contact us:
strings.a11y_promise_text: BetterLegazpi is committed to ensuring that our digital services are accessible to all citizens, regardless of ability. We view accessibility not as a feature, but as a fundamental right.
